output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error in our own systems. When the Tallis product record for mandarins was created on 1 Aug, it was copied from the avocado record and kept avocado's 7.0°C carriage temperature. Our specification for mandarins is 4.0°C. Every Meridane container booked through Tallis (K3, K4, K6, K8, K9) was sent at 7.0°C and ran at 7.0°C, and every one was rejected. The 4.0°C containers (K1, K2, K5, K7) all passed, including those packed with Pellacor, so the new fungicide isn't the cause. Meridane's units held the setpoint we gave them, so a claim against them would fail. Lower Serra fruit made up 28–40% of every container, accepted ones included, so suspending those growers isn't justified. I'm about 90% sure of this. Next steps, in order: (1) Correct the mandarin record in Tallis today. (2) Have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct to 4.0°C. (3) Add a check that compares the reefer setting with the product specification before each submission. (4) Hold off on the cargo claim, the grower suspension and the Pellacor reversal. Independent loggers are a reasonable extra safeguard. Review the sign-off process, not individual blame.
